co_alderfer_three_sisters_park.blurb: Alderfer/Three Sisters Park is a county open space in the Front Range foothills near Evergreen, at about 7,500 feet among ponderosa pines. The climbing is almost entirely bouldering on hard granite blocks and domes, from V0 to about V10, with a big supply of V1 to V5 problems and only a sprinkling of roped lines. Style ranges from crimpy faces and technical slabs to a few steep, overhung boulders. The Eggs suit easier problems, the Work and Play Area collects mid-grade lines, and Tortuga spreads harder classics over a wider zone. The east side is shady forest, while the west side is open and sunny. Spring and autumn give the best friction, and the trail network can confuse first-timers.

az_east_stronghold.blurb: East Stronghold is the eastern half of Cochise Stronghold in the Dragoon Mountains of southeast Arizona, a maze of rugged canyons and pink granite domes, towers and slabs. Bouldering and trad make up most of the climbing, with sport routes as a smaller third; many trad lines are multipitch and some are committing. Roped grades cluster between 5.9 and 5.11, with a spread of easier lines, and the boulders run from V0 to V10 or so. The Rockfellow Group is the standout formation, Lebowski Wall holds much of the sport, and East Stronghold Bouldering covers the problems. Fall through spring is the busiest stretch, since summers are extremely hot, and winter sun is a draw.

ky_muir_valley.blurb: Muir Valley is a preserve in the Red River Gorge of east-central Kentucky, with more than thirty separate walls of sandstone cliffs. The climbing is mostly bolted sport on steep, overhanging stone, with a smaller share of trad. Grades run from easy up to 5.14, but the weight sits in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, so strong climbers are well served, and moderate leaders still find a fair set of easier walls such as Bruise Brothers Wall, The Boneyard and The Stadium. The grades here have a reputation for running soft, although that should not be taken for granted. Many routes are single pitch on cliffs well under 200 feet tall.

nm_new_mexico_other_northern_areas.blurb: This grouping holds the climbing of northern New Mexico away from the main population centers, between I-40 and the Colorado border. The rock changes with the location: sandstone in the east and west, granite through the middle, and basalt and other volcanic stone elsewhere. Roy is the largest area, a remote bouldering destination in Canadian River country cut into fragile Dakota sandstone, with classic problems from V1 to V7 and the best season running from mid-fall to mid-spring. Sugarite Canyon State Park and Waterflow lean toward trad, Ortegas is all boulders, and there is a little winter ice near Navajo Dam. Overall, bouldering and trad dominate, with some sport.

wa_olympics.blurb: This region stretches from the tip of the Olympic Peninsula to the Columbia River and mixes coastal bouldering, remote mountaineering and sport crags. Bouldering and sport are the two biggest groups, followed by trad, scrambles, alpine routes and a few top-ropes. Elwha River is the best-known sport area, with sandstone and conglomerate in a river canyon and routes from about 5.7 to 5.12. Cape Disappointment sits on basalt sea stacks and wave-cut cliffs at the mouth of the Columbia, often mossy, with a blend of sport, trad and highball boulders. Olympic National Park and Olympic National Forest hold alpine objectives plus more sport. Roped grades run up to 5.12, and boulders to about V7.

wa_tieton_river.blurb: Tieton River climbing is strung out over about twenty miles of the river drainage on the east slope of the south Cascades. The rock is andesite in columns, a relative of basalt, and the routes are split roughly evenly between trad and sport, with a smaller bouldering scene. The lower canyon, including Royal Columns and The Bend, favors cracks, while higher crags such as Lava Point and The Cave carry more bolts. Trad is strongest around 5.10 and sport around 5.11, with a decent base of moderates. The lower canyon is semi-arid with sagebrush, and the upper crags sit in conifer forest. It stays dry, works well in winter sun, and most crags get some shade, which makes summer climbing bearable.
